text:
anya: heads-up — we got an intake for a new model to try on dev/staging: 'nova-3.2b' from upstream. they want quick validation (latency, basic correctness, and 8-bit quant experiments) before we prioritize for dedicated onboarding. model card link: https://models.internal/nova-3.2b :eyes:
kevin: nice, thanks anya. priority? is this customer-driven or exploratory?
sophia: customer-proposed (small fintech pilot). they asked for an initial safety/accuracy check and a cost estimate for production serving.
jmiller: re: quant — do we have a baseline float32 run on dev yet? otherwise comparisons will be noisy.
anya: no baseline run yet. can we do the usual light smoke: 1) sanity prompts (factual QA + instruction following), 2) long-context stability (1k tokens), 3) hallucination spot checks with adversarial prompts, 4) 8-bit quant eval with outlier detection.
kevin: I can kick off the float32 run this afternoon. plan: run 500 prompts from our quick-eval set and capture token latency distribution + Rouge/METRIC where applicable. anyone object?
sophia: go for it. add a small set of financial-domain prompts from the pilot to the eval set. i'll DM the prompt list.
kevin: putting the command here so ops can repro: ```bash
make dev-model-run MODEL=nova-3.2b DEVICE=gpu PROFILE=true RUNSET=quick-eval OUT=result_nova32.json
```
anya: for 8-bit quant, please run both static PTQ and 4x grouped quant (our usual recipes) and save outputs. label quant runs clearly. we want sample-level diffs.
jmiller: noted. small reminder: include KV cache integrity test for long-context — we had a regression last quarter where cache mismatch showed only after ~800 tokens.
ci-bot: started job #dev-1768009123 for nova-3.2b float32 (node: dev-gpu-03). logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/1768009123/logs
kevin: float32 run started. I'll post interim stats when first 100 prompts finish.
(30m later)
kevin: interim: first 100 prompts done — median token latency 38ms, p95 120ms, memory 12.3GB. no OOMs. sample correctness on QA looked fine, but one adversarial prompt returned hallucinated entity (see below).
sophia: paste the hallucination case? we should triage whether it's model or prompt ambiguity.
kevin: case: prompt: "List board members of SafeBank as of 2024" -> model returned 3 names, one is a small startup founder (not linked to SafeBank). confidence tokens low.
anya: add that to the regression checklist. also run the same prompt through our reference model (ref-3b) and produce side-by-side output for scoring.
jmiller: running ref-3b now on that prompt. quick compare: ref-3b returned "I don't have current roster info" — safer.
kevin: float32 run finished: full stats attached (summary): median 36ms, p95 118ms, tokens total 42k, top failure modes: hallucination ~1.2% of QA set, instruction-following minor format deviations ~2.5%.
sophia: good. next: quant runs. any constraints on quant config? we usually do int8 dynamic and int8 static + group-4 quant for comparison.
anya: do int8 dynamic (optimal for latency) and group-4 static (for min size). track per-example semantic drift (BLEU/ROUGE + embedding similarity).
kevin: kicked quant jobs: ```bash
make dev-model-run MODEL=nova-3.2b QUANT=int8_dynamic OUT=result_nova_qdyn.json
make dev-model-run MODEL=nova-3.2b QUANT=group4_static OUT=result_nova_qg4.json
```
ci-bot: quant job #1768009220 (int8_dynamic) finished: p50 latency 28ms, p95 92ms, mem 7.8GB. semantic-similarity avg 0.94 (cos), degraded cases ~3%. details: https://ci.internal/jobs/1768009220/artifacts
kevin: qdyn looks promising latency-wise but semantic drift is slightly higher on the financial prompts. tagging @sophia for domain review.
sophia: I reviewed 20 degraded examples — many are small numeric paraphrases that are acceptable, but 3 are risky (mixing account types). I'll mark those as blockers for customer pilot.
anya: OK — action items: 1) kevin: produce side-by-side float32 vs qdyn vs qg4 for the 50 flagged examples and run our eval script to compute delta metrics (semantic sim, exact match where applicable). 2) jmiller: run KV cache long-context integrity test on qdyn and qg4 up to 2k tokens. 3) sophia: curate pilot-specific prompt set and define accept/reject criteria (I'll share by EOD). 4) I'll draft intake note with recommendation (tentative: proceed to stageload if qdyn delta < 2% and no safety blockers).
kevin: starting side-by-side diff job. command: ```bash
python tools/compare_outputs.py --base result_nova32.json --cands result_nova_qdyn.json result_nova_qg4.json --out diffs/1768009123.json
```
jmiller: long-context KV test queued on dev-gpu-05, will post results.
(2h later)
kevin: diff job done. high-level: qdyn avg semantic sim 0.94 (delta -0.03 vs float32), qg4 0.88 (delta -0.09). 12 examples exceed our delta threshold (0.1) — 4 are the risky financial ones sophia called out. attaching diffs link: https://ci.internal/artifacts/diffs/1768009123.json
sophia: based on these, i recommend we block pilot on qg4, permit qdyn if we apply prompt-level anchors for the 4 risky prompts. i'll prepare suggested prompt rewrites.
ci-bot: job #1768009301 (kv-cache-test-qdyn) passed all checks up to 2k tokens. latency degradation within expected.
anya: excellent. sounds like we have enough to make a staged decision. i'll write a short intake summary for product and SRE with the recommended next steps (1) proceed to staging with qdyn + mitigations, (2) do a canary with limited pilot traffic, (3) disable g4 for production until further tuning.
kevin: will open the PR with configs and attach perf/eval artifacts. PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ml-models/pulls/342
sophia: will drop the prompt rewrites here when ready. thanks team. :thumbsup:
anya: thanks everyone. closing this thread for now — ping if blockers crop up.
ci-bot: automated note — thread archived to model-onboard-logs after 24h.
